sets.oddNote: A carrot is a root. Tomatoes, cucumbers and peppers grow from the flower and carry the seeds, which makes them fruits.
Sydney is Australia's biggest city, but the capital is Canberra.
Sharks are fish. Whales, dolphins and seals breathe air and feed their young milk.
An ant is an insect with six legs. Adult spiders, scorpions and ticks have eight.
Brazilians speak Portuguese.
Ireland has been an EU member since 1973. The UK left in 2020.
A desert is defined by how little rain or snow falls, not by heat. Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth. The Amazon is rainforest.
Venus is a planet, even though it's often called the morning or evening star.
You can't survive without a liver.
Peanuts are legumes, like peas and lentils. An almond is the seed of a fruit related to the peach.
Koalas are marsupials. They're sometimes called koala bears, but they aren't bears.
Seahorses and eels are fish. Dolphins are mammals.
A strawberry isn't a berry. Its 'seeds' are really tiny fruits, and the red flesh is the swollen base of the flower. Bananas, grapes and tomatoes are true berries.
A catfish is a fish. Starfish are echinoderms, jellyfish are cnidarians and cuttlefish are molluscs.
Neptune is a full planet. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
Quartz is silicon and oxygen. Diamond, graphite and graphene are all pure carbon.
Hydrogen is a flammable gas that reacts readily. Noble gases barely react at all.
Centipedes are myriapods. Insects have six legs; centipedes have dozens.
Canada drives on the right.
Pavlova is named after the ballerina Anna Pavlova. The others are named after Hamburg, the village of Cheddar and the town of Bakewell.
The platypus is a monotreme, one of the few mammals that lay eggs.
Lagos is Nigeria's biggest city, but the capital moved to Abuja in 1991.
Peru has a long Pacific coastline. Ethiopia lost its coast when Eritrea became independent.
Killer whales and pilot whales belong to the dolphin family. The blue whale is a baleen whale.
All four are botanically fruits. Cucumbers, butternut squash and pumpkins are gourds. Apples are in the rose family.
Tomatoes, potatoes and aubergines are nightshades. Onions are related to garlic and leeks.
A hazelnut is a true nut. Brazil nuts, cashews and almonds are the seeds of other kinds of fruit.
A blueberry is a true berry. Raspberries, blackberries and loganberries are clusters of tiny fruits.
Saturn's are the famous ones, but Jupiter and Uranus have rings too. Mars has none.
Triceratops was a dinosaur. Flying pterosaurs and swimming plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs lived alongside them but weren't dinosaurs.
An adder is a snake. The slow worm looks like one but is a legless lizard.
The hammer, anvil and stirrup are the three tiny bones of the middle ear.
Bamboo and sugar cane are giant grasses. Palms are a separate family.
Au (aurum), Ag (argentum) and Pb (plumbum) come from Latin. Zinc is Zn.
Brazil is named after brazilwood, a tree. The others are named after Simón Bolívar, Prince Philip (later Philip II of Spain) and the House of Saud.
Switzerland uses the Swiss franc. Kosovo uses the euro without any agreement with the EU, and Vatican City and Andorra use it under formal deals.
Almaty is Kazakhstan's biggest city, but the capital moved to Astana in 1997.
Egypt drives on the right.
Pearls grow in molluscs, amber is fossilised tree resin and coral is built by tiny animals. Ruby is a mineral.
51 looks prime but is 3 × 17.
A cherry is a drupe, with a single hard stone. Avocados, aubergines and kiwis are berries.
Despite the name, horseshoe crabs are closer to spiders. Coconut crabs, woodlice and barnacles are all crustaceans.

sets.link: Share a land border with France
sets.oddNote: Suriname and Brazil border French Guiana, and the Kingdom of the Netherlands borders France on the island of Saint Martin. Portugal's only neighbour is Spain.
Magenta is named after the 1859 Battle of Magenta in Italy, sienna after Siena, and turquoise means 'Turkish'. Scarlet was originally the name of a fine cloth.
Denim is 'de Nîmes', calico comes from Calicut in India and muslin from Mosul.
The bikini is named after Bikini Atoll. The others are named after an acrobat, a chemist and a duke.

Mary Anderson patented the windscreen wiper, Josephine Cochrane built the first commercially successful dishwasher and Stephanie Kwolek invented Kevlar. Nylon came from Wallace Carothers's team at DuPont.
Pythons kill by squeezing. Male platypuses have venomous spurs, and the slow loris is the only venomous primate.
Their blood carries oxygen with copper rather than iron, which turns it blue when oxygenated. Sharks have red blood like ours.
Octopuses, squid and cuttlefish each have three hearts. A snail has one.
The microwave came from a melted chocolate bar near a radar set, Post-its from a failed glue, and superglue from a failed gunsight material.
Romanian comes from Latin. Albanian is a branch of its own.
Shampoo, pyjamas and bungalow come from Hindi and Urdu. Ketchup most likely comes from a Chinese word for fish sauce.
Tycoon comes from Japanese.
Polonium is named after Poland. Einsteinium is named after Albert Einstein.
Hyenas look like dogs but sit on the cat side of the carnivore family tree, with meerkats and mongooses.
Rhinos look elephantine but are closer to horses. The manatee, the dugong and the small, furry hyrax really are the elephant's closest relatives.
South Africa has three capitals. Bolivia's government sits in La Paz but Sucre is the constitutional capital. The Dutch capital is Amsterdam, but the government is in The Hague.
Uranus's moons are named after characters from Shakespeare and Pope. Ganymede orbits Jupiter.
Yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium are all named after Ytterby, where their ore was found.
Finnish and Hungarian are Uralic languages, and Basque is related to no other living language. Lithuanian is Indo-European, like English.
New York is at about 40.7°N, level with southern Italy. Porto, Barcelona and Rome are all further north. Athens is at 38°N.
Birds are living dinosaurs, so ostriches and pigeons count. Pterodactyls were flying reptiles, not dinosaurs.
Bats fly but they are mammals, not birds. The penguin and ostrich can't fly, yet they are every bit as much birds as the robin.

Polar bears live only in the Arctic, so wild penguins and polar bears never meet. The Arctic tern, despite its name, flies south each year to spend the southern summer at the edge of the Antarctic ice.
Blood is a fluid tissue, not an organ. Skin, though, is an organ, and your largest one.
Teeth are not bones. They are made of enamel and dentine, and a chipped tooth can't heal the way a broken bone does.
The kidney is a filtering organ, not a muscle. The tongue, heart and diaphragm, the sheet you breathe with, are all muscle.
Newts look like lizards but are amphibians, laying eggs in water and starting life as tadpoles. The tortoise, shell and all, is a reptile.
Sloths hang from trees like apes, but they are not primates. Humans, gorillas and lemurs all are.
Puffins look like little penguins but fly well, flapping up to 400 times a minute. Penguins, ostriches and emus can't fly.
The funny bone isn't a bone at all. That jolt comes from knocking the ulnar nerve against your elbow.
Bats are the only one here with powered flight, flapping their wings. The others can only glide.
T. rex died out about 66 million years ago, long before any humans. People hunted mammoths and woolly rhinos, and sailors met the dodo.
The octopus has a large brain and is famously clever. Jellyfish and corals get by with simple nerve nets, and sponges have no nerve cells at all.
The liver sits on your right, under the ribs. Your heart, stomach and spleen all lean to the left.
Eggshell is about 95% calcium carbonate, the same mineral as chalk. Hair, nails and feathers are all built from the same protein, keratin.
Rabbits are lagomorphs, not rodents, with a second pair of small upper front teeth. The beaver and the prickly porcupine are rodents, like the hamster.

In chickens it is the hen that sits on the eggs. Seahorse fathers carry eggs in a pouch, emperor penguin fathers incubate them through the winter, and male midwife toads carry strings of eggs wrapped round their back legs.
Starfish are echinoderms, related to sea urchins. The octopus is a mollusc like the oyster; it has lost the shell its cousin the nautilus still carries.
Seaweed is algae, not an animal. Sponges, corals and barnacles spend their adult lives fixed in place, but they are all animals.
Hedgehogs give birth to live young. The spiny echidna looks like a hedgehog but, like the platypus, is a mammal that lays eggs.
Baboons are monkeys and have tails. The small, swinging gibbon is an ape, with no tail.
The coelacanth was thought to have died out with the dinosaurs until one was caught off South Africa in 1938. It is still alive today.
Despite starring in Jurassic Park, T. rex lived in the Cretaceous. It lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
The electric eel makes electricity, not light. Fireflies, krill and lanternfish all make their own light.
The sperm whale hunts squid with its teeth. The whale shark, the biggest fish of all, sieves tiny plankton just like the blue whale and the basking shark.
The fibula is the thin bone in your lower leg. The radius and ulna are in your forearm, the humerus above them.
Squirrels don't hibernate. They stay active all winter, living off food they buried in autumn.

The blue morpho's shimmering blue comes from the microscopic structure of its wing scales, not from pigment or food. Flamingos, scarlet ibises and salmon get their pink from pigments in what they eat.
The leafy seadragon is a fish, a close cousin of the seahorse. The other three dragons are lizards.
A gecko can regrow a lost tail but not a leg. Axolotls regrow whole limbs, and crabs and lobsters regrow legs when they moult.
Horses don't chew the cud. They ferment grass in a large pouch near the end of the gut instead of a many-chambered stomach. Cows, deer and giraffes are all ruminants.
Shield bugs look like beetles but are true bugs, sucking sap through a beak-like mouth. The glow-worm, despite its name, is a beetle, as are fireflies and ladybirds.
The okapi is a species in its own right and the giraffe's closest living relative. Its stripes have nothing to do with zebras.
Antlers are bone, grown and shed every year. Rhino horn, hooves and whale baleen are keratin, like your fingernails.
Pigeons coo but can't copy words. The common starling is a gifted mimic of speech and other sounds.
Raccoons have their own family, shared with coatis. Badgers, otters and the wolverine are all mustelids, the weasel family.
The swordfish is a bony fish. The sawfish, despite the similar snout, is a ray with a cartilage skeleton like sharks.
Mice are rodents. Shrews look like mice but belong with moles and hedgehogs, in an order called Eulipotyphla.
The axolotl, nicknamed the Mexican walking fish, is a salamander, an amphibian. The mudskipper, which walks on mud, is a true fish.
Jellyfish are cnidarians, kin to corals. Starfish, urchins and sea cucumbers are echinoderms, which are closer relatives of us than of jellyfish.
Dragonflies are not true flies. True flies have only one pair of wings, and crane flies and hoverflies are among them along with the housefly.
Termites are not close relatives of ants. They are social cockroaches, while ants evolved from wasps.

Seahorses stay the same sex for life, though the males carry the young. Clownfish all start as males and the biggest in a group turns female, while many parrotfish and wrasse switch from female to male.
The kakapo, a flightless parrot from New Zealand, is critically endangered but still alive. The dodo, the Carolina parakeet and the passenger pigeon have all been wiped out.
Plesiosaurs died out 66 million years ago with the dinosaurs. Crocodiles, turtles and snakes lived alongside dinosaurs and made it through.
Bushbabies look like lemurs but live on the African mainland. Ring-tailed lemurs, the fossa and leaf-tailed geckos are found wild only in Madagascar.
The flying squirrel is a rodent. The American opossum is a marsupial with a pouch, like the gliding sugar glider of Australia.
Only the earthworm is a real worm. Woodworm are beetle grubs, shipworms are clams and the slow worm is a legless lizard.
Elephants live up to about 70 years. Bowhead whales pass 200 and Greenland sharks may reach 400.
The robin is a true native. Rabbits were brought over to be farmed, probably by the Normans, pheasants come from Asia and grey squirrels from North America.
Manatees have only six neck bones. A giraffe has seven, the same number as you and a mouse.
The jaguar roars like lions, tigers and leopards. Cheetahs and clouded leopards can't, and nor can snow leopards, despite being in the same genus as the roarers.
The flying fox is a large fruit bat. The prairie dog is a ground squirrel and the guinea pig is a rodent, not a pig.
Frogs date back only about 250 million years. Sharks, scorpions and jellyfish were all around before the first trees, about 385 million years ago.
The vampire squid eats drifting 'marine snow', not blood. The vampire finch of the Galapagos pecks seabirds and drinks their blood, and male vampire moths can pierce skin with their tongues.
Dogs sleep with their whole brain. Dolphins, mallards and frigatebirds can rest one half of the brain while the other stays alert; frigatebirds even do it while flying.
Pigs have very few working sweat glands, so 'sweating like a pig' is wrong. They wallow in mud to cool down instead.
Sea lions have small ear flaps, which is one way to tell them from true seals. Common seals and penguins have only ear holes, and snakes have no outer ears at all.
Enamel contains no living cells, so once it is lost it never grows back. The liver can regrow from as little as a quarter of its size.

sets.link: One eye moves across the head
sets.oddNote: Skates are flat rays with eyes on top from birth. Young plaice, sole and turbot start out like normal fish, then one eye migrates to join the other.
The femur is a single bone. Your sacrum is five fused vertebrae, each hip bone is three fused bones, and the skull is over 20 bones knitted together, with only the lower jaw left free.
Dogs vomit easily. Horses, rats and rabbits essentially can't, so anything they swallow has to go all the way through.
Owls hunt by listening but don't echolocate. Oilbirds click to find their way through pitch-dark caves, and dolphins and sperm whales hunt by sonar.
A cobra is venomous: it injects its toxin with a bite. The others are poisonous to touch or eat, and the pitohui is a bird with toxic feathers.
Cobras have no heat-sensing pits. Rattlesnakes do, vampire bats have heat sensors on their noses to find a vein, and mosquitoes home in on the infrared warmth of skin.
Octopuses have just two eyes. A horseshoe crab has around ten, a box jellyfish 24, and a scallop can have up to 200.
A mealworm is the grub of a darkling beetle. Silkworms, woolly bears and inchworms all grow up to be moths.
The tapeworm is a flatworm, from a different animal phylum. The leech, despite its looks, is a segmented worm like the earthworm and the ragworm.
The tiny money spider is a real spider. Camel spiders are solifuges, spider crabs are crabs and sea spiders aren't even arachnids.
Male elephant seals can be several times heavier than females. Female sparrowhawks are much bigger than males, and some male anglerfish are tiny.
The tawny owl is native. Little owls were released in Victorian times, muntjac deer came from China and American mink escaped from fur farms.
The iguana is a lizard. Crocodiles are more closely related to birds than to lizards.
Rhinos are odd-toed, like horses. Whales evolved from even-toed hoofed mammals, and the hippo is their closest living relative.
The fossa of Madagascar looks like a cat but is related to mongooses. The lynx, ocelot and serval are true wild cats.
Kangaroos don't have fingerprints. Koalas do, and theirs are so like ours that they are hard to tell apart under a microscope.
Dogs can taste sweet things. Cats, sea lions and dolphins have a broken sweet-taste gene, so sugar means nothing to them.
The cow has one stomach with four compartments. The platypus, seahorse and goldfish have no stomach at all; food passes straight to the intestine.
Pigs lack the reflective layer behind the eye that makes eyes glow in torchlight. Cats, alligators and sharks have one.

The pangolin looks like an armadillo, but its closest relatives are carnivores such as cats and dogs. Armadillos and both kinds of sloth, along with anteaters, form one American group, the xenarthrans.

sets.link: Alive when the pyramids were built
sets.oddNote: Sabre-toothed cats died out about 10,000 years ago. Woolly mammoths survived on an Arctic island until about 4,000 years ago, after the Great Pyramid was built, and the moa and Madagascar's elephant bird lasted into medieval times.
The kinkajou looks like a monkey but is a member of the raccoon family. The aye-aye is an odd-looking lemur.
The hummingbird hawk-moth sips nectar with a long tongue. Adult mayflies, botflies and atlas moths have no working mouthparts and live off reserves built up as larvae.
The pancreas makes digestive juices and insulin. Tonsils, the spleen and the thymus all help fight infection as part of the lymphatic system.
The tuatara of New Zealand looks like a lizard but is the last survivor of a separate reptile order. Its lineage split from lizards over 200 million years ago.
The true mole is related to hedgehogs. Golden moles and elephant shrews just look like moles and shrews; they are African relatives of elephants.
Stegosaurus is a dinosaur. Dimetrodon, often mistaken for one, was on the branch that led to mammals, including mice and the echidna.
The giant panda is a bear. The red panda has its own family, closer to raccoons and skunks.
The moray is a true eel. The electric eel isn't an eel at all; it is a knifefish, related to catfish and piranhas.
The kea, an alpine parrot, flies well. Its cousin the kakapo is the world's only flightless parrot.
Eagles and falcons look alike but aren't close kin. DNA shows falcons are closer to parrots such as the budgie and to songbirds such as the canary.
The sea urchin is an echinoderm. The blob-like sea squirt has a notochord and nerve cord as a larva, putting it in our phylum, the chordates, along with lampreys and hagfish.
Hummingbirds can't sense electric fields. Bumblebees can sense the tiny charge on flowers, and the platypus finds prey with electric sensors in its bill.
The spider crab is a true crab. King crabs evolved from hermit crabs, and porcelain crabs are their relatives too.
Grass snakes lay eggs, often in compost heaps. Boa constrictors, Jackson's chameleons and, in Britain, common lizards give birth to live young.
Tibia is Latin for a flute or shinbone. Muscle means 'little mouse', cochlea 'snail' and coccyx 'cuckoo', after its beak-like shape.
The retina is packed with blood vessels. The cornea has none and takes its oxygen straight from the air.
Achilles was a hero of Greek myth. The others are named after real Renaissance and 17th-century anatomists: Eustachi, Falloppio and Willis.

The pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs. The pulmonary vein brings it back full of oxygen, and before birth the umbilical vein brings oxygen-rich blood from the placenta.
The bison belongs with cattle. The musk ox, despite its name, is closer to sheep and goats.
Magpies build their own nests. Like cuckoos, cowbirds and honeyguides trick other birds into raising their chicks.
Roald Dahl wrote under his real name. Mark Twain was Samuel Clemens, Lewis Carroll was Charles Dodgson and Dr Seuss was Theodor Geisel.
Anne Boleyn was a queen only by marriage to Henry VIII. Anne, Mary I and Victoria were reigning monarchs.

sets.link: Not from the land they protect
sets.oddNote: St David was Welsh, born in Pembrokeshire. George came from the eastern Roman Empire, Patrick from Roman Britain and Andrew from Galilee.
A griffin is part lion, part eagle. The centaur is half man, the hippocampus half fish and the hippogriff half eagle, but all three are half horse.
Ra was the Egyptian sun god. Poseidon, Neptune and the Norse god Njord were all gods of the sea.
Merlin was King Arthur's wizard and adviser, not a knight.
The cornet is brass. The saxophone and flute count as woodwind despite being metal, because of how the sound is made, not what they're made of.
Humpty Dumpty has its own tune. The other three share an 18th-century French melody, 'Ah vous dirai-je, maman'.
Rodin's The Thinker isn't in the Louvre: the best-known cast is at the Musée Rodin, elsewhere in Paris. The other three are all in the Louvre.
The Little Mermaid was written by the Dane Hans Christian Andersen. Hansel and Gretel, Snow White and Rumpelstiltskin are Grimm fairy tales.
Hamlet is set in Denmark. The others take place in Verona, Venice and Padua.
Oxford grew up as a Saxon town, first recorded in 912. London, York and Bath were Roman Londinium, Eboracum and Aquae Sulis.

sets.link: Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
sets.oddNote: Rome's Colosseum was never one of the Seven Wonders, despite sounding like the Colossus of Rhodes.
Car comes from the Latin carrus, a wagon, not from a longer word. Bus is from omnibus, taxi from taximeter cab and van from caravan.
The cracker was invented in London by sweet-maker Tom Smith in the 1840s. The tree, calendar and wreath all came from Germany.

sets.link: In The Twelve Days of Christmas
sets.oddNote: The robin is on plenty of Christmas cards but not in the song. Partridges, swans a-swimming and geese a-laying all are.
Lord Raglan was a baron, never an earl. The sandwich, Earl Grey tea and the Derby are named after the Earl of Sandwich, Earl Grey and the Earl of Derby.

The hooded sweatshirt was first made by Champion in the 1930s for labourers working in freezing upstate New York. Trench coats were made for army officers, aviators for pilots and cargo trousers for British battledress in 1938.
Elizabeth of York was Henry VIII's mother, the wife of Henry VII. Catherine of Aragon, Anne of Cleves and Catherine Parr were three of his six wives.
Rubens was Flemish, from Antwerp in what is now Belgium, and was born in Germany. Van Gogh, Rembrandt and Bosch were all born in what is now the Netherlands.
The Minotaur was killed by Theseus. Heracles slew the lion and the Hydra and dragged Cerberus up from the underworld alive.
Tutankhamun's mask is kept in Egypt. The Rosetta Stone, though Egyptian too, is in London.
Beethoven was German, born in Bonn, though he lived in Vienna. Mozart was born in Salzburg, now in Austria, Haydn in Lower Austria and Schubert in Vienna.
Go comes from China. Chess grew from the Indian game chaturanga, snakes and ladders from moksha patam and ludo from pachisi.
Apollo kept the same name in Greece and Rome. The Greeks knew the others as Zeus, Aphrodite and Artemis.
There's no solid evidence Robin Hood ever existed; he comes from medieval ballads. The other three were real, documented criminals.
HMS Victory has never sunk and sits in dry dock in Portsmouth. The Mary Rose sank in 1545 and was raised in 1982.
Hot cross buns were sold by London street-sellers by the 1730s, a century before Victoria. The Penny Black (1840), the first Christmas card (1843) and afternoon tea (1840s) all began in her reign.
Conan Doyle was born in Edinburgh to an Irish Catholic family. Stoker and Wilde were born in Dublin, C. S. Lewis in Belfast.
SOS doesn't stand for anything, not even 'Save Our Souls'. It was picked because the Morse code is easy to send and recognise.
X-rays got their name because Wilhelm Röntgen didn't know what they were, so he used X for unknown.
Turkish switched from Arabic script to the Latin alphabet in 1928, so it now reads left to right.

sets.link: Executed inside the Tower of London
sets.oddNote: Mary, Queen of Scots was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle in Northamptonshire. The other three were beheaded within the Tower of London.
The £2 coin is round. The 20p and 50p have seven curved sides and the current pound coin has twelve.
Long John Silver was invented by Robert Louis Stevenson for Treasure Island. The other three really sailed and plundered.

sets.link: Won the Nobel Prize in Literature
sets.oddNote: Tolstoy was nominated several times but never won. Churchill won the literature prize in 1953 for his writing and speeches.
Victoria was born at Kensington Palace, despite her German family. Henry II was born in Le Mans, Richard II in Bordeaux and George I in Hanover.
Machu Picchu was built around 1450. Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325, after teaching began at Oxford (1096), Notre-Dame was begun (1163) and the present Westminster Abbey was begun (1245).
The lava lamp feels very 1970s but was invented in 1963. The Rubik's Cube and Hello Kitty date from 1974 and Trivial Pursuit from 1979.
The Starry Night has never been stolen. The Mona Lisa was taken from the Louvre in 1911, The Scream twice in Oslo, and the Ghent Altarpiece many times.
Klimt's The Kiss is in the Belvedere in Vienna. The National Gallery owns one of Van Gogh's Sunflowers, alongside Constable and van Eyck.
Museum comes from the Greek Muses. Cereal is from Ceres, volcano from Vulcan and martial from Mars.

Oates really did say 'I am just going outside and may be some time', according to Scott's diary. Holmes never says 'Elementary, my dear Watson' in the books, Kirk never says 'Beam me up, Scotty', and there's no evidence Marie Antoinette said 'Let them eat cake'.
Hans Christian Andersen never studied medicine. Conan Doyle, Chekhov and Somerset Maugham all qualified as doctors.
Turkish delight, or lokum, was perfected in Ottoman Istanbul. Panama hats are made in Ecuador, Chinese checkers was invented in Germany and Arabic numerals came from India.

Santa grew out of St Nicholas folklore, and was red long before Coca-Cola's adverts. The Michelin Guide was made to sell tyres, Guinness's record book was a giveaway to promote its beer and Rudolph was created for a US department store in 1939.
US notes are printed on a cotton and linen blend. Australia pioneered polymer notes in 1988, and Romania and the Bank of England now use them for all notes.
The jigsaw dates from the 1760s, when London mapmaker John Spilsbury cut up maps. The teddy (1902), crossword (1913) and sliced bread (1928) are all newer.
Victoria was crowned in 1838. Edward V vanished in the Tower, Jane reigned nine days and Edward VIII abdicated before his coronation.
Bread is native Old English. Knife, egg and window (Norse vindauga, 'wind eye') came into English from the Vikings' Old Norse.
Canoe comes from Taíno, a Caribbean language, via Spanish. Easel is Dutch for donkey, cookie is from koekje and yacht from jacht.
Toboggan comes from Mi'kmaq, a First Nations language of eastern Canada. Kayak, igloo and anorak are Inuit words.

The bowler was made in 1849 for gamekeepers on a Norfolk estate, by the hatters Thomas and William Bowler. The others are named after Balaclava in Crimea, Lord Raglan and the Earl of Cardigan, all from the Crimean War.

Jack-o'-lantern was 1660s slang for a will-o'-the-wisp, using Jack as an any-man name; only later did it mean a carved lantern. The Catherine wheel honours St Catherine, the ladybird 'Our Lady' (the Virgin Mary), and the St Bernard the alpine hospice of St Bernard of Menthon.
Baker Street, home of Sherlock Holmes, isn't on the board. Vine Street, a tiny street near Piccadilly Circus, is.
Monopoly is American. Cluedo came from Birmingham, Meccano from Liverpool and Spirograph from a British engineer in 1965.
French women got the vote only in 1944. New Zealand led in 1893, followed by Australia (for most women) in 1902 and Finland in 1906, all before Britain in 1918.
Osiris is shown as a man, usually wrapped like a mummy. Anubis has a jackal's head, Horus a falcon's and Thoth an ibis's.

sets.link: On the royal coat of arms
sets.oddNote: Wales has no symbol on the royal arms: no daffodil, leek or dragon. The lions stand for England and Scotland, the unicorn for Scotland and the harp for Ireland.
Nelson's Column really is topped by Nelson. Big Ben is the bell, not the tower, Eros is really his brother Anteros, and Cleopatra's Needle is more than a thousand years older than Cleopatra.
Picasso named Guernica himself. Whistler called his 'Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1', Constable showed his as 'Landscape: Noon', and The Night Watch is a nickname for a militia portrait.

Tokyo Tower was based on the Eiffel Tower but designed by Tachū Naitō and finished in 1958, long after Eiffel's death. Eiffel's firm built the Paris tower, the Garabit Viaduct and the iron skeleton inside the Statue of Liberty.

The Golden Gate has been International Orange since it opened. Liberty was shiny copper before it turned green, the Eiffel Tower was first painted Venetian red and Tower Bridge was chocolate brown until 1977.
Newt gained an N: 'an ewt' became 'a newt'. The reverse happened to 'a napron', 'a nadder' and 'a noumpere'.
Pineapple was first a word for a pine cone. Muscle is Latin for little mouse, porcelain comes from an Italian word for a cowrie shell meaning piglet, and dandelion is the lion's tooth.
Frisbee is still a registered trademark of Wham-O. Linoleum (1878), escalator (1950) and yo-yo (1965) were all ruled ordinary words that anyone can use.
Ferrari is named after its founder, Enzo Ferrari. Barbie was Ruth Handler's daughter Barbara, Mercedes was Emil Jellinek's young daughter, and Barrie named Peter Pan after Peter Llewelyn Davies.
The fez is named after Fez, a real city in Morocco. The trilby comes from a novel, the fedora from a play and the tam o' shanter from a Burns poem.
Dollar comes from the thaler, a coin named after Joachimsthal, a Bohemian valley. Pound, peso and shekel all began as units of weight.
Ultramarine was ground from lapis lazuli, a stone. Carmine comes from cochineal insects, sepia from cuttlefish ink and Tyrian purple from sea snails.
Kilt comes from a Scandinavian word for tucking up clothes. Whisky is from uisge beatha, 'water of life', bog from bog, 'soft', and trousers from triubhas.
Didgeridoo isn't from an Aboriginal language: it's thought to be an English word imitating the instrument's sound. Boomerang, koala and budgerigar come from Aboriginal languages of New South Wales.
The knight has always been a horseman. The queen began as a weak royal adviser, the bishop as an elephant and the rook as a chariot.

Machiavelli wrote The Prince in 1513, a few months after he was released from prison and torture. Bunyan wrote in Bedford gaol, Malory called himself a 'knight prisoner' and Marco Polo dictated his travels in a Genoese jail.

sets.link: Closer to us than the pyramids
sets.oddNote: Alexander died in 323 BC, slightly nearer the building of the Great Pyramid (about 2560 BC) than to today. The other three lived after the halfway point.
Edison's phonograph came in 1877, a year after the telephone. The fax was patented in 1843, before even the telephone's inventor was born.
Kodak is a made-up word; George Eastman liked the letter K. Volvo means 'I roll', ludo 'I play' and video 'I see'.

sets.link: Not made of what they're called
sets.oddNote: Bone china really does contain bone ash. Pencil lead is graphite, catgut is usually sheep intestine and kitchen tin foil is aluminium.
Lego bricks were designed as toys from the start. Play-Doh began as wallpaper cleaner, bubble wrap as textured wallpaper and the chainsaw as a bone-cutting tool for childbirth in 1780s Scotland.

Admiralty Arch has stood in the same spot since 1912. Marble Arch moved from Buckingham Palace, Temple Bar went to Hertfordshire and back to London, and Wellington Arch was rebuilt up the road in the 1880s.
Great Expectations carried Charles Dickens's name. Austen, Mary Shelley and Walter Scott all first published those books without theirs.

The Mars bar is named after the Mars family who made it, not the Roman god. Nike is the Greek goddess of victory, AFC Ajax is named after the Greek hero and NASA's Apollo programme after the god Apollo.
Botticelli painted The Birth of Venus on canvas, unusual for 1480s Florence. The Mona Lisa is on poplar, the other two on oak.
Pavilion comes from the Latin for butterfly, after the shape of tents. Pea, cherry and marquee came from 'pease', 'cherise' and 'marquise', which English speakers took for plurals.
Bird widened: it once meant only a young bird. Deer meant any animal, meat any food and girl any child.
Tepee comes from Lakota, a Siouan language of the Great Plains. Moose, raccoon and moccasin come from Algonquian languages of the east coast.
Pen comes from the Latin penna, a feather. Pencil meant little tail (a fine brush), vanilla little pod and pupil little doll.
Italy's anthem has well-known lyrics. The anthems of Spain, Kosovo and San Marino have no official words.
The asterisk is a drawn star; its name is Greek for little star. The ampersand is a joined-up Latin 'et', the pound sign an L for libra and the percent sign a shorthand for 'per cento'.
The Sagrada Família is by Antoni Gaudí, a Catalan working in his native Catalonia. The others were designed by a Dane, a Chinese-born American and a Finnish-born American.
Rupee comes from Sanskrit for wrought silver. Yen, yuan and won all come from the same Chinese character for round, as in round coins.
The harpsichord plucks its strings. The piano, like the dulcimer and the Hungarian cimbalom, hits them.
Roman cavalry rode without stirrups, which reached Europe centuries later. Romans had concrete, underfloor hypocausts and blocks of flats called insulae.
Vivaldi was born in 1678. Bach, Handel and Scarlatti were all born in 1685.
Salmon has no special status. A statute of 1324, under Edward II, makes whales and sturgeon royal fish belonging to the Crown, and porpoises were later added.
Linear A, used in Minoan Crete, is still undeciphered. Linear B, its successor, was cracked in 1952 and turned out to be early Greek.
The Cuerdale Viking hoard was dug up by workmen repairing a riverbank in 1840, long before metal detectors. The other three were found by hobby detectorists.
A kimono is sewn from several panels. The sari, toga and dhoti are single lengths of cloth wrapped and draped around the body.
The wendigo is a monster from Algonquian folklore in North America. Kappa, tengu and kitsune all come from Japanese legend.

sets.link: Written or scripted by Roald Dahl
sets.oddNote: Mary Poppins was created by P. L. Travers. Dahl wrote The BFG and the screenplays for the Bond film You Only Live Twice and Chitty Chitty Bang Bang.
Brazil nuts grow high up in rainforest trees, packed inside heavy woody pods. Peanut pods push down into the soil to ripen.
A prune is a dried plum. Raisins, sultanas and currants are all dried grapes of different varieties.
Mead is brewed from honey. Sake is brewed from rice, mochi is pounded sticky rice and arancini are fried risotto balls.
Polenta is cornmeal, made from ground maize. The other three are all potato dishes.
Jasmine tea is usually green tea scented with jasmine blossom, so it is real tea. Peppermint, ginger and chamomile are herbal infusions with no leaves from the tea plant.
Tahini is a paste of ground sesame seeds, though it often goes into hummus. Gram flour is ground chickpeas.
Star anise looks like a flower but is the dried, star-shaped fruit of an evergreen tree. Saffron is the dried stigmas of a crocus flower, and rosewater and elderflower cordial are made from blossoms.
The sensitive plant folds its leaves when touched, but it doesn't eat insects. The other three trap and digest them.
Rooibos is a South African bush, not the tea plant, and is naturally caffeine-free. Kola nuts, which gave cola its name, are rich in caffeine, and dark chocolate contains a little.
Honey is made by bees from flower nectar. Rum, Brazilian cachaça and demerara sugar all come from sugar cane.
A toffee apple really is an apple. Wine gums contain no wine, sweetbread is offal rather than bread, and Welsh rarebit, originally 'Welsh rabbit', is cheese on toast.
A banana plant isn't a tree. Its 'trunk' is tightly rolled leaf stalks, making it the world's largest herb.
Cow parsley is edible, but it looks so like hemlock that foragers are wary of it. Hemlock, foxglove and deadly nightshade can all kill.
Naan is traditionally leavened with yeast, which makes it puff up. Arepas, corn tortillas and chapatis are made with no raising agent.
Moss is a plant that makes food from sunlight. Truffles, chanterelles and puffballs are fungi, which aren't plants at all.
Limoncello is an Italian liqueur made from lemon zest. Greek ouzo, Italian sambuca and French pastis all taste of aniseed.
A pineapple grows on a low, spiky plant on the ground, one fruit at a time. Grapes, kiwi fruit and passion fruit all grow on climbing vines.
Gelatine is made from animal collagen. Agar, its vegetarian substitute, is extracted from red seaweed, and Welsh laverbread is cooked seaweed.
Seitan is made from wheat gluten, so it contains no soya. Edamame are young soya beans, and tempeh and miso are fermented soya.
Maple syrup is boiled-down sap of the maple tree. Tequila, mezcal and agave syrup all come from the agave plant.
The broad bean is a true bean, a legume. Coffee 'beans' are the seeds of a cherry-like fruit, cocoa beans are seeds from a pod and vanilla 'beans' are the seed pods of an orchid.
Aloe vera is a succulent but not a cactus; it's in the same family as red-hot pokers. Dragon fruit grows on a climbing cactus.
The satsuma is named after Satsuma, an old province of Japan. Granny Smith, Bramley and Logan were all real people.
The Swiss roll isn't named after anyone, and probably isn't Swiss. Caesar Cardini, Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya and Giuseppe Garibaldi were real people.

Brown sauce gets its tang from tamarind and vinegar, with no fish. Worcestershire sauce is made with anchovies, Provençal tapenade traditionally includes them, and Gentleman's Relish is mostly anchovy.
Pilsner is a lager, made with bottom-fermenting yeast. Dark stouts and porters are ales, just like pale IPAs.
Scones rise thanks to baking powder, not yeast. Crumpets get their holes from yeast bubbles.
A pear has under a tenth of the vitamin C of an orange. Weight for weight, peppers, broccoli and blackcurrants all beat oranges.
Allspice is a single spice, the dried berry of a Caribbean tree. It got its name because it tastes like several spices at once.
Grape seeds don't contain these compounds. Apple pips, apricot kernels and cherry stones all contain amygdalin, though you'd need a lot to be harmed.
Black pepper comes from the berries of a tropical vine, Piper nigrum. Paprika, cayenne and chilli flakes are all dried capsicum peppers.
Prosciutto is salted and air-dried, not smoked. Lapsang souchong tea is dried over pine fires, and a chipotle is a smoked jalapeño.
Ivy only uses trees for support and doesn't feed on them. Mistletoe and dodder tap into their hosts, and rafflesia lives entirely inside a vine.

sets.link: Same egg, flour and milk batter
sets.oddNote: Crumpet batter is raised with yeast and usually has no egg. Yorkshire puddings, pancakes and toad in the hole share one simple batter.
Earl Grey is named after a person, Charles Grey, a 19th-century prime minister. Ceylon is the old name for Sri Lanka.
The lime is a true citrus fruit. Lemongrass is a grass, lemon balm is a mint and lemon verbena is a South American shrub.
Walnuts are in the walnut family, with pecans and hickories. Almonds belong to the rose family, as close cousins of peaches and apricots.
The sunflower is in the daisy family. Rapeseed, the yellow crop in British fields, is a close relative of cabbage and turnip.
Fenugreek is a legume, in the pea family. Cumin seeds come from a small plant in the carrot family, a cousin of parsnip and celery.
Cinnamon is the bark of a tree in the laurel family. Cardamom pods come from a plant in the ginger family.
Bamboo is a giant grass. Rattan, used for wicker furniture, comes from climbing palms.
Yerba mate is made from a South American holly. Matcha, oolong and smoky lapsang all come from the same tea plant, Camellia sinensis.
Seagrass is a true flowering plant that happens to live in the sea. Kelp is a brown alga, mushrooms are fungi and a lichen is a fungus living with algae.
Brussels sprouts are buds too, but leaf buds, not flower buds. Cloves, capers and globe artichokes are all unopened flower buds.
Yew is a softwood, because it's a conifer, though its wood is very hard. Balsa is one of the lightest woods there is, yet it counts as a hardwood.
The mango comes from South Asia. Chillies and cashews are both from the Americas and only reached India in the 1500s.
Peanuts come from South America. Kiwi fruit were once called Chinese gooseberries, and peaches were first grown in China.
Green tea is green because the leaves are heated to stop them darkening. Green peppers, olives and peppercorns are simply unripe.
A rose's colour is in its petals. The red of a poinsettia is in special leaves called bracts, and its real flowers are the tiny yellow bits in the middle.
Nutmeg is a seed. Tonic water gets its bitterness from quinine, which comes from the bark of the cinchona tree.
A banana is botanically a berry. The coconut is not a nut but a drupe, a stone fruit like an olive or a plum.
Gorgonzola is made from cow's milk. Roquefort, the other blue, is made from sheep's milk.
Tofu is soya milk set into curds with no fungus involved. Quorn is grown from a fungus, Marmite is yeast extract and soy sauce is brewed with a mould.
Calvados is an apple brandy from Normandy. Cognac and pisco are grape brandies, and grappa is made from the skins and pips left after winemaking.
Coconut oil comes from the white 'meat', which is actually part of the seed. Olive, avocado and palm oils are pressed from the fleshy outer part of the fruit.
Sweet potato is safe to eat raw. Raw kidney beans contain a toxic protein, cassava can release cyanide and unripe ackee is poisonous.
Meringue is a foam: air whipped into egg white. Butter is an emulsion too, of water droplets held in fat, and vinaigrette is oil and vinegar shaken together.
Custard gets its yellow from egg yolks, or from colouring in custard powder. Traditional paella and Marseille's bouillabaisse both use saffron.

sets.link: Can be grown in the dark
sets.oddNote: Lettuce needs light to grow. Forced rhubarb is grown in dark sheds, chicory is forced in darkness and white asparagus is kept under soil.
Sauternes is sweet because of a mould on the grapes, not added spirit. Port, sherry and Madeira all have brandy or grape spirit added.
The olive belongs to a different family. Avocados are in the laurel family, alongside cinnamon and the bay tree.
Papaya is unrelated. Mangoes, pistachios and cashews share a family with poison ivy, and mango skin can cause a similar rash.
Black pepper is in an unrelated family. Sichuan pepper is the dried husk of a citrus relative, which explains its lemony aroma.
The potato is a nightshade. The sweet potato is in the bindweed family, alongside the morning glory.
Barley is a cereal grass. Buckwheat isn't wheat or even a grass; it's a relative of rhubarb and Japanese knotweed.
The turnip is a different species, Brassica rapa. Kale, kohlrabi and Brussels sprouts were all bred from wild cabbage, Brassica oleracea.
Spinach is a related but separate species. Beetroot, chard and sugar beet are all varieties of one plant, Beta vulgaris.
'Maize' comes from Taíno, a Caribbean language. Tomato, avocado and chilli come from Nahuatl words used by the Aztecs.
The sardine is probably named after the island of Sardinia. Salad, sauce and salami all come from the Latin 'sal', meaning salt.
Farfalle means 'butterflies'. Orecchiette means 'little ears', linguine 'little tongues' and capellini 'little hairs'.
Chillies get their heat from capsaicin. Wasabi, horseradish and hot mustard get their nose-tingling kick from allyl isothiocyanate.
A pineapple stops ripening once it's picked, so it won't get any sweeter. Bananas, mangoes and papayas keep ripening and sweetening after picking.
Dahlias come from Mexico, where they are the national flower. Wild apples still grow in Kazakhstan, tulips come from Central Asian mountains, and carrots were first farmed in that region.
Kiwi fruit were named after New Zealand's national bird. Tangerine comes from Tangier, damson from Damascus and currant from Corinth.
Hawthorn is native. Sycamores arrived from Europe around the 1500s, horse chestnuts from the Balkans and sweet chestnuts probably with the Romans.
Scots pine keeps its needles all year. Larch, dawn redwood and bald cypress are conifers that go bare every winter.
A crocus grows from a corm, a solid swollen stem, not a bulb of layered leaves. Saffron comes from a crocus.
No major drug comes from oak. Foxglove gave us the heart drug digoxin, and periwinkle and yew give cancer drugs.
A sweet potato is a swollen root. A potato is a swollen underground stem, which is why it has 'eyes' that sprout shoots.
A nectarine is not a peach-plum cross; it's a smooth-skinned peach. The garden strawberry is a hybrid of two American wild species.
Prosecco usually gets its bubbles in large pressurised tanks. Champagne, cava and crémant are fermented a second time in the bottle.
Wild rice is a grass, though not true rice. Quinoa, buckwheat and chia are seeds of broad-leaved plants.
Eucalyptus is in the myrtle family, despite its minty smell. Teak, the timber tree, belongs to the mint family.
Coffee is in the same family as gardenias. The cocoa tree belongs to the mallow family, with cotton and hibiscus.
Lavender is in the mint family. Ash trees and lilac are close relatives of the olive.
The pomelo is one of the original wild citrus species. The orange is a pomelo-mandarin cross, and the grapefruit is pomelo crossed with orange.
A blackberry forms from a single flower. A mulberry, fig or jackfruit forms from a whole cluster of flowers fused together.
A raspberry's flesh grows from the flower's ovaries, as a true fruit should. Strawberry, pear and rose hip flesh grows from other flower parts.
Sunflowers are pollinated by bees. Many agaves, including the source of tequila, rely on nectar-feeding bats, as do durian and baobab.

sets.link: Fruit grows straight from the trunk
sets.oddNote: Coconuts hang in bunches at the top of the palm. Cocoa pods, jackfruit and jabuticaba sprout straight from the trunk.
Black tea is often called fermented, but its leaves darken through oxidation by the plant's own enzymes. Cocoa beans must be fermented by microbes to make chocolate.
Broccoli flowers carry both sexes. Only female holly trees have berries, only female ginkgos drop smelly seeds, and asparagus plants are male or female too.
Wheat uses the ordinary C3 process. Maize, sugar cane and sorghum use C4, a more efficient type of photosynthesis suited to heat.
The carrot is a dicot, with two seed leaves. Onion, pineapple and vanilla, an orchid, sprout a single seed leaf, like grasses.
Magnolia is a flowering plant, one of the oldest. Ginkgos, cycads and junipers are gymnosperms; a juniper 'berry' is a fleshy cone.
The date palm is a true palm. The Torbay palm and ponytail palm are both in the asparagus family, and the traveller's palm is related to bananas.
Linen comes from the stems of the flax plant. Cotton is seed hair, coir is coconut husk and kapok is fluff from a tree's seed pods.
Tulip comes from a Persian word for turban. Hyacinthus was a youth loved by Apollo, Iris the rainbow goddess and Paeon the gods' physician.
Yams belong to their own family. Cassava, the source of tapioca, is a spurge, like the rubber tree and castor oil plant.
Wheat is grown from seed. Saffron crocuses and supermarket bananas are sterile, and every navel orange tree is grafted from one Brazilian original.
Greenland is the world's largest island, but it isn't an independent country. It is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.

sets.link: On the island of Great Britain
sets.oddNote: Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom but not of Great Britain, which is the island shared by England, Scotland and Wales.
Iceland is a Nordic country, but Scandinavia strictly means Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
Glasgow is Scotland's biggest city, but Edinburgh is the capital.

sets.link: King Charles is head of state
sets.oddNote: India has been a republic with its own president since 1950. Canada, Australia and New Zealand still have the British monarch as head of state.
Switzerland sits in the middle of the EU but has never joined it.
Iranians mainly speak Persian (Farsi). Iran is not an Arab country.
Singapore is a fully independent city-state. Puerto Rico belongs to the US, Hong Kong to China and Tahiti to France.
Puerto Rico is a US territory, not a state. Its people are US citizens, but residents cannot vote in presidential elections.
Portugal feels Mediterranean, but its whole coast faces the Atlantic.
Sardinia belongs to Italy, even though it sits just south of French Corsica.
Cambridge is on the River Cam. The Thames flows through Oxford, Windsor and London.
China spans about five geographical time zones, yet the whole country runs on Beijing time.
Bermuda is out in the open Atlantic, roughly level with South Carolina and far north of the Caribbean.
The Masai Mara is in Kenya. Kilimanjaro, Zanzibar and Ngorongoro are all in Tanzania.
Belfast is in Northern Ireland, part of the UK, so it uses the pound.
France swapped the franc for the euro in 2002 (only its Pacific territories still use the CFP franc). The Swiss, Rwandan and Djiboutian francs are still in use.
Cambodia has a coastline on the Gulf of Thailand. Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country.
Spain borders France, Portugal, Andorra, Gibraltar and Morocco (at Ceuta and Melilla). Portugal touches only Spain, South Korea only North Korea and Qatar only Saudi Arabia.

Japan has been called Nihon or Nippon for over a thousand years; only its formal title, the Empire of Japan, was dropped in 1947. Sri Lanka was Ceylon until 1972, Thailand was Siam until 1939, and Iran asked the world to stop calling it Persia in 1935.
The Bahamas became independent in 1973. Bermuda, the Falklands and Montserrat are still British territories.
Prague stands on the Vltava, not the Danube.
The Danube is only Europe's second-longest river. The Volga, flowing through Russia, is longer.
The Black Sea connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosporus, so it is a true sea. The other three have no outlet to the ocean, which makes them lakes.
The Matterhorn was carved by glaciers from folded rock. Kilimanjaro, Fuji and Etna are all volcanoes.
Donegal is in the Republic of Ireland, even though it contains the most northerly point on the island.
The Isle of Man is a Crown dependency with its own parliament, Tynwald. It is not part of the UK.
Tenerife is one of the Canary Islands, in the Atlantic off the coast of Africa.
India is less than half the size of Australia. Brazil, often thought smaller, is about 10% bigger.
Angel Falls lies wholly inside Venezuela. Niagara is shared by the US and Canada, Victoria by Zambia and Zimbabwe, and Iguazu by Argentina and Brazil.
French Guiana is part of France, so it is in the EU and uses the euro.
The -chester, -caster and -cester endings come from the Latin castra, a camp. Birmingham means 'home of Beorma's people'.
Britain leans to the west as it goes north, so Edinburgh, Liverpool and Glasgow are all west of Bristol. Manchester is east of it.
Gretna Green is just over the border in Scotland. Hadrian's Wall never marked the border and lies wholly in England.
Eswatini is almost encircled by South Africa, but it also borders Mozambique.
Morocco is wholly in Africa. Egypt reaches into Asia through the Sinai, and Turkey and Kazakhstan both have land in Europe.
Ecuador is Spanish for 'equator'. Paraguay, Senegal and Jordan all take their names from rivers.
Venezuela means 'little Venice', after houses on stilts the explorers saw. Colombia honours Columbus, Mauritius Maurice of Nassau and the Seychelles a French finance minister.
Fiji has its own Fiji dollar. Ecuador, El Salvador and East Timor all use the US dollar as their official currency.
The Czech Republic still uses the koruna. Croatia joined the euro in 2023 and Bulgaria in 2026.
Canada dropped the Union Jack for the maple leaf in 1965. Fiji's national flag, Hawaii's state flag and British Columbia's provincial flag all still carry it.
Bosnia has about 20 km of Adriatic coast around the town of Neum. Serbia, Paraguay and Zambia have no coastline at all.
Sumatra is wholly Indonesian. Hispaniola is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, Timor by Indonesia and East Timor, and Tierra del Fuego by Argentina and Chile.

sets.link: Share a land border with Russia
sets.oddNote: Japan is close to Russia but only across the sea. Poland borders Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, and North Korea has a short border on the Tumen River.
Moscow is well north of London. Calgary, Kyiv and Vancouver all lie further south.
Most of mainland Spain lies west of Greenwich, but Madrid uses Central European Time, an hour ahead of the UK. Only Spain's Canary Islands are on GMT.
Freetown was named for the freed slaves who settled there. Monrovia honours US President James Monroe, Georgetown King George III and Washington George Washington.
Mumbai has never been India's capital. Rio was Brazil's until 1960, Karachi Pakistan's until 1959 and Philadelphia the US capital in the 1790s.
Kilimanjaro is wholly in Tanzania. Everest's summit is on the Nepal–China border, K2's on the Pakistan–China border and the Matterhorn's on the Swiss–Italian border.
Helvellyn is only England's third-highest peak. Snowdon tops Wales, Scafell Pike England and Slieve Donard Northern Ireland.
Lake Baikal is entirely in Russia. Geneva is shared by Switzerland and France, Titicaca by Peru and Bolivia, and Superior by the US and Canada.
The Sahel is the semi-arid strip of grassland south of the Sahara. It gets too much rain to count as desert.
Peru stops just short of the equator, which runs through neighbouring Ecuador and Colombia.
Reykjavík is about 270 km south of the Arctic Circle, which barely touches Iceland at all.
Romania is slightly smaller than the UK. New Zealand, Japan and Ecuador are all bigger.
Egypt has the Nile. Saudi Arabia, Libya and Kuwait have no river that flows all year round.
Reading is far bigger than St Asaph, Wells or St Davids, but its bids for city status have all failed. It remains a town.
Nepal abolished its monarchy in 2008. Andorra has two co-princes, and Lesotho and Bhutan have kings.
Lake Michigan is the only Great Lake entirely inside the United States.
The Northern Territory is a territory, not a state, so the federal parliament can override its laws.
Costa Rica means 'rich coast'. The Canaries are named after dogs (Latin canis), the Caymans after caimans and Cameroon after the Portuguese for prawns.
Honduras means 'depths' in Spanish. Belarus means 'White Rus', Vermont comes from the French for 'green mountain', and Blackpool is named after a dark, peaty pool.
French is widely used in Morocco but not official. The official languages are Arabic and Amazigh (Berber).
Jamaica's flag is a gold saltire with green and black. Albania's has a double-headed eagle, Mexico's an eagle and Papua New Guinea's a bird of paradise.

sets.link: Share a land border with China
sets.oddNote: Thailand is close to China but separated by Myanmar and Laos. Afghanistan touches China through the narrow Wakhan Corridor.
Minsk is south of Moscow. Edinburgh and Glasgow are both slightly further north than the Russian capital, and Bergen much further.
Las Vegas is east of Los Angeles. Reno, in Nevada, is surprisingly further west than LA because California's coast bends east as it goes south.
Nepal's clocks are 5 hours 45 minutes ahead of GMT, a quarter-hour offset. India, Iran and Myanmar are all offset by a half hour.
Lima sits near sea level on the Pacific coast. Quito, Addis Ababa and Nairobi are all well above Ben Nevis's 1,345 m.
Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory. Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man are Crown dependencies, a different status.
The Faroes belong to Denmark but chose to stay out of the EU. Réunion, Madeira and the Canaries are in the EU despite lying off Africa.
The US makes no territorial claim in Antarctica and does not recognise anyone else's. Norway, France and Chile all claim slices.
Ireland is in the EU but kept its own border controls, sharing a travel area with the UK instead. Switzerland and Liechtenstein are in Schengen without being in the EU.
The Volga flows east and then south to the Caspian Sea. The Nile, Rhine and Lena all flow northwards.
Etna is about 3,300 m, well short of Mont Blanc's 4,800 m. Elbrus, Ararat and Mount Kenya are all over 5,000 m.
Even the bottom of the Grand Canyon is hundreds of metres above sea level. The Sea of Galilee is about 210 m below it.
Miami is about 2 degrees north of the Tropic of Cancer. Hong Kong, Honolulu and Mumbai all lie inside the tropics.
Oswestry is in Shropshire, England, despite its Welsh name, Croesoswallt. Monmouth, Wrexham and Chepstow are in Wales.
Lewis is in the Outer Hebrides. Skye, Mull and Islay are in the Inner Hebrides.
John o' Groats is not the most northerly point; Dunnet Head is. Lizard Point is the most southerly and Lowestoft the most easterly.
Myanmar switched to driving on the right in 1970, despite its British colonial past. Mozambique and East Timor drive on the left despite their Portuguese past.
Gibraltar is British but drives on the right, like Spain. Suriname drives on the left despite being a former Dutch colony.
Guyana is English-speaking. Equatorial Guinea, a former Spanish colony, added Portuguese as an official language in 2010.
Java has more people than any other island but is much smaller than Great Britain. Baffin, Honshu and Canada's Victoria Island are all larger.
Andorra is an independent country. Kaliningrad is cut off from Russia, Llívia is a Spanish town surrounded by France, and Cabinda is separated from Angola.
K2 is only second-highest. Everest is highest above sea level, Mauna Kea tallest from base to peak, and Chimborazo's summit is furthest from Earth's centre.
K2 is in the Karakoram range, not the Himalayas. Nanga Parbat marks the Himalayas' western end.
Louth is in Leinster. Ulster has nine counties, and Donegal, Cavan and Monaghan are the three in the Republic.
New Zealand is named after Zeeland in the Netherlands. Nova Scotia is 'New Scotland', Calgary is named after a bay on Mull and Dunedin is Gaelic for Edinburgh.
Sweden is named after a people, the Swedes. Australia means 'southern land', Austria 'eastern realm' and Vietnam 'southern Viet'.

sets.link: Part of the Kingdom of Denmark
sets.oddNote: Åland belongs to Finland, even though its people speak Swedish.
Tahiti is French. Easter Island and the Juan Fernández Islands belong to Chile and the Galápagos to Ecuador.
Uganda was a British protectorate. Mozambique was Portuguese, Rwanda Belgian and Gabon French, yet all three joined the Commonwealth.
The Zambezi flows into the Indian Ocean. The Volga ends in the Caspian, the Jordan in the Dead Sea and the Okavango soaks into the Kalahari.
Portugal lies entirely west of Greenwich. The meridian runs through the UK, then France, Spain, Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Togo and Ghana.
The Cape of Good Hope is not Africa's southern tip; Cape Agulhas is. Cape York is Australia's northern tip and Cabo da Roca mainland Europe's western tip.
Brisbane takes its name from the river, which was named after Sir Thomas Brisbane, a governor. Regina honours Queen Victoria, Adelaide Queen Adelaide and Charlottetown Queen Charlotte.
Venezuela's coast is all Caribbean and Atlantic. Honduras has a short Pacific shore on the Gulf of Fonseca.
France and the UK are linked only by the Channel Tunnel. Spain borders Gibraltar, and Cyprus borders the UK's Sovereign Base Areas.
Ivory Coast is named after the ivory trade. Sierra Leone means 'lion mountains', Montreal is named after Mount Royal, and Gibraltar comes from the Arabic for 'Tariq's mountain'.
The Moon makes no light of its own. Moonlight is sunlight bouncing off its grey rock.
A tornado is a narrow funnel of wind spun out of a single thunderstorm. Hurricanes, typhoons and cyclones are one kind of giant ocean storm with regional names.
Tin is a pure element. Bronze is copper plus tin, brass is copper plus zinc, and steel is iron plus carbon.
Household bleach is strongly alkaline. Cola is surprisingly acidic, thanks to added phosphoric acid.
An oxygen tank exploded on the way out, so Apollo 13 swung round the Moon and came home without landing.
A seismometer measures the ground shaking during earthquakes, not the weather.
Paper is made from wood pulp. Chips start as silicon refined from quartz sand.
Shiny silicon is a metalloid, not a metal. Sodium, calcium and magnesium are all silvery metals, though we mostly meet them locked up in compounds such as salt and chalk.

sets.link: Not made of what they're called
sets.oddNote: Rock salt really is salt, and a rock. Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide, kitchen 'tin' foil is aluminium and pencil 'lead' is graphite and clay.
Copper isn't magnetic. Iron, nickel and cobalt are the three everyday metals a magnet will grab.
A diesel train burns its fuel inside the engine's cylinders, with no steam involved. A nuclear power station is, at heart, a very elaborate kettle driving steam turbines.
Most starfish have five arms. Honeycomb cells, snowflakes and most Giant's Causeway columns are six-sided.
Magenta isn't in the rainbow. Your brain creates it when your eyes see red and blue light with no green.
Dew is liquid water that condenses on cool surfaces. Hail, snow and frost are all ice.
A knot is a speed: one nautical mile per hour. A light-year, despite the name, is a distance.
Venus has no moons at all. Mars has two small ones, Phobos and Deimos.
Glass has a jumbled atomic structure with no regular crystal pattern. 'Crystal' glassware borrows its name from rock crystal, not from chemistry.
Jupiter is a third denser than water. Saturn is so light that, in a big enough bath, it would float.
Uranus is named after Ouranos, the Greek god of the sky. It's the only planet named after a Greek god.
An F1 car tops out at around a third of the speed of sound. The crack of a whip is a tiny sonic boom from its tip.
Table salt is sodium chloride, with no carbon. Limestone is calcium carbonate.
Most TV remotes send pulses of infrared light. Microwaves are short radio waves, so an oven, a radar dish and a key fob all use the same kind of wave.

sets.link: Kept in time by a pendulum
sets.oddNote: An hourglass runs on falling sand, with nothing swinging. The Great Clock in Big Ben's tower is fine-tuned by adding or removing old pennies on its pendulum.
No horse has been to space. Fruit flies flew in 1947, a French cat in 1963, and two tortoises circled the Moon in 1968, before any human.
No dog was aboard. In 1783 the Montgolfier brothers sent a sheep, a duck and a cockerel aloft at Versailles.
A fridge magnet is a permanent magnet and needs no electricity. A loudspeaker cone is pushed by an electromagnet coil.
A classic hard drive has spinning platters and a swinging read arm. A USB stick stores data in solid-state chips.
The Plough is an asterism, a star pattern inside the constellation Ursa Major (the Great Bear).

sets.link: Stronger than steel, weight for weight
sets.oddNote: Lead is soft and weak. Spider silk is stronger than steel of the same weight.
Lemonade stays dark under UV. Tonic water glows blue because of its quinine, teeth glow under club lights and scorpions glow blue-green.
A lodestone is a naturally magnetic rock, so it works by magnetism, not static. Photocopiers and laser printers use static charge to make toner powder stick to paper.
William Hoover was a leather-goods maker who bought the patent for an upright electric cleaner from its inventor, a janitor called Murray Spangler.
Titan is Saturn's largest moon. Io, Europa and Callisto orbit Jupiter.
A kite's opposite sides aren't parallel. A square counts as a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram.
A geode is a hollow rock lined with crystals, never alive. A coprolite is fossilised dung.

sets.link: Sunlight bent by water or ice
sets.oddNote: An aurora is made by charged particles from the Sun hitting the upper air. Halos and sun dogs come from sunlight bent through ice crystals.
Cling film is plastic made from oil. Cellophane and rayon are both made from wood pulp, and cork is tree bark.
Joseph-Ignace Guillotin only proposed a more humane execution machine. A surgeon, Antoine Louis, designed it.
The Web was invented by a British scientist, but at CERN near Geneva, Switzerland, in 1989.
Sudoku first appeared in a US puzzle magazine in 1979 as 'Number Place'. Japan popularised it and gave it the name.
Sapphire isn't a programming language. Python, Ruby and Swift are, and Python is named after Monty Python, not the snake.
Memory foam really was developed for NASA, in 1966, to cushion aircraft seats. The Space Pen was developed privately by Paul Fisher, and NASA then bought it.
The barcode was patented in 1952, but shops couldn't scan one until 1974.
Radio came in the 1890s, after the 1876 telephone. The first fax machine was patented in 1843.
Velcro was inspired by burrs stuck to a Swiss engineer's dog. The microwave oven came out of wartime radar research.
A ruby gets its red from traces of chromium. Mars, Uluru and terracotta are coloured by iron oxide, which is rust.
No tennis ball has been to the Moon. Alan Shepard hit golf balls there, Apollo 15 left a falcon feather and Apollo 11 left a small gold olive branch.
The Gulf Stream is an ocean current. A monsoon is a seasonal wind that brings the rains, and the sirocco is a hot wind off the Sahara.
Lava is molten rock, which makes it a liquid. Plasma is gas so energised that electrons are stripped from its atoms, as in the Sun and inside glowing gas tubes.

sets.link: Not the colour in their name
sets.oddNote: The White House really is white. Flight recorders are bright orange, the Golden Gate Bridge is 'International Orange' and Greenland is mostly ice.
Tides are driven by the gravity of the Moon and Sun. Wind comes from sunshine heating the air unevenly.
A neutron is made of three quarks, so it isn't fundamental. Electrons, quarks and neutrinos can't be split any further, as far as anyone knows.

sets.link: Regular ones tile a floor alone
sets.oddNote: Regular pentagons always leave gaps. Only equilateral triangles, squares and regular hexagons tile a flat floor on their own.
The Orion Nebula is a cloud of gas inside our own galaxy. The 'clouds' of Magellan are separate galaxies.
Sand won't burn. A fine cloud of flour, custard powder or sawdust can explode, which is why flour mills fear sparks.
Limestone is a sedimentary rock. Heat and pressure turn it into marble, as they turn mudstone into slate.
Plaster of Paris is calcium sulfate, made from gypsum. Marble, eggshell and seashell are all calcium carbonate.
Chlorine is Cl. Potassium is K, from its Latin name kalium, and tungsten is W, from wolfram.
Emerald gets its green from traces of chromium or vanadium. Malachite, turquoise and azurite owe their colour to copper, the metal that turned the Statue of Liberty green.
Titanium is named after the Titans of Greek myth, not Saturn's moon. Selenium is named after the Moon, tellurium after the Earth and cerium after Ceres.
Candle wax shrinks as it sets, which is why a dip forms round the wick. Gallium and bismuth swell like water does when it freezes.
Sapphire is corundum, the same mineral as ruby. Green emerald, blue aquamarine and pink morganite are all beryl.
Jade is a different mineral, nephrite or jadeite. Amethyst, citrine and tiger's eye are all quartz.
Quartz grows as six-sided columns. Salt, pyrite and galena naturally form near-perfect cubes.
Granite cooled slowly deep underground, which is why its crystals are big. Pumice, obsidian and basalt come out as lava.
Magnetite is about as hard as a steel knife. Talc, graphite and gypsum can all be scratched with a fingernail.
A kettle heats a plain metal element. A contactless card has no battery: the reader's magnetic field powers its chip.
The 12-sided pound coin is wider corner to corner than side to side. Round coins are equally wide every way, and so is the curved seven-sided 50p, so coin slots can measure it.
James Webb was not an astronomer. He ran NASA in the 1960s.
Red Betelgeuse is huge but cooler than the Sun. Star colour shows temperature, and blue-white stars are the hottest.
Orion never hosts the Sun. Ophiuchus does, from late November to mid-December, even though it's not a star sign.
Sodium is named after soda. Chlorine means pale green, iodine violet and rubidium deep red.
Copper is lighter than lead. Gold, platinum and tungsten are all far denser.
Real lino is made from linseed oil, cork dust and wood flour. Vaseline is a by-product of oil drilling.
Lego is Danish. Bluetooth was developed at Ericsson in Sweden, though it is named after a Danish king.
Lapis lazuli is blue all through and was ground up to make ultramarine paint. Blue eyes and morpho wings get their blue from light scattering in their structure.
Golden syrup flows the same however you push it. Ketchup and toothpaste thin out when squeezed, and quicksand turns liquid when disturbed.
A classic pretzel has three holes. To a mathematician a straw has just one hole, and a mug is the same shape as a doughnut.
A spiral galaxy's arms wind out in a flat spiral, not a helix. A spiral staircase is, strictly, a helix.
Perspex is an acrylic plastic. Obsidian is volcanic glass and fulgurite is glass made when lightning melts sand.
LED bulbs contain no mercury, unlike the fluorescent tubes they replace. Amalgam fillings are about half mercury, cinnabar is mercury's main ore and big fish like tuna build it up in their flesh.
Tungsten is Swedish for 'heavy stone'. Niobium is named after Niobe, tantalum after her father Tantalus and vanadium after the Norse goddess Vanadís.
Caesium is nearly twice as dense as water, so it sinks, then explodes. Lithium, sodium and potassium are light enough to float as they fizz.
The Geminids come from Phaethon, a rocky asteroid. The Orionids are dust from Halley's Comet.
A cube is all squares. A classic 32-panel football, like any ball stitched from hexagons and pentagons with three at each corner, needs exactly 12 pentagons.
Zinc was being smelted centuries earlier, in India. Davy used electricity to split out magnesium, calcium and barium in 1808.

Light reflects inside raindrops to make a rainbow, but only partly: in a round drop it can never be totally reflected. Total internal reflection makes diamonds sparkle and bounces light round binocular prisms.
Indigo dye comes from plants or a factory. Shellac is a resin from lac bugs, and red carmine is crushed cochineal insects.
Neon colours signs, not fireworks. Strontium salts burn red, barium green and copper blue.
Sugar's atoms share electrons rather than forming charged ions, so it isn't a salt. Chalk is the salt calcium carbonate.
Fizzy drinks are charged with carbon dioxide. Crisp packets are flushed with nitrogen to stop the crisps going stale.
America's Space Shuttle, first flown in 1981, was the first reusable orbital spaceplane. The Soviets launched the first satellite, space station and robot Moon rover.

Charon was named by its discoverer, James Christy, partly after his wife Charlene. Pluto's name was suggested by an 11-year-old Oxford girl, and both rovers were named by school pupils in essay contests.
Opportunity ran on solar panels and lasted until dust storms smothered them. The others run on heat from decaying plutonium.
A square pyramid mixes square and triangle faces. Platonic solids use one regular shape for every face.
Oxygen was found by chemists collecting gases. Helium was first spotted as a mystery yellow line in sunlight, years before it was found on Earth.
Iodine stays solid until about 114°C. Mercury and bromine are liquid at room temperature, and gallium melts below 30°C, so it can melt in your hand.
Venus's air is mostly carbon dioxide. Saturn's moon Titan has a thick nitrogen atmosphere, like Earth's.
Enceladus is only about 500 km across. Europa, Triton and Titan are all bigger than Pluto.
